question.leadin: A meeting in this city was interrupted by Napoleon's escape from Elba.
question.text: Name this host of an 1815 meeting that established the balance of power of Europe in the 19th century, the capital of Austria.
question.clue: Following one battle, cannons captured from the defeated Ottomans were melted down into a bell for this city's St. Stephen's Cathedral.

swap.text: What nephew of Franz Josef was killed in that attack?
swap.answerHtml: Archduke Franz Ferdinand [or Francis Ferdinand; prompt on partial answer]
swap.clue: His wife was never permitted in the royal carriage, as a condition of his marriage to the lower-class woman after he became heir apparent following the death of his cousin Rudolf and father Charles Louis.

question.leadin: Genetic defects such as severe underbite and large chins recurred in this family due to inbreeding.
question.text: Name this central European noble family which included Maximilian I, Marie Antoinette, Charles V, and Maria Theresa.
question.clue: The founder of this house gained significant parcels of land after his victory at the Battle of Marchfeld, and the death of a later member of this house served as the extinction of its non-Styrian branch.

swap.text: The Spaniards were led by Philip II and other kings of this dynasty. This royal house also had an Austrian branch and sported a namesake "jaw" due to incest.
swap.clue: In the 19th century, this family took the title "King of Lombardy-Venetia".

question.leadin: Answer the following about the 1814 and 1815 Congress of Vienna.
question.text: The Congress was chaired by this Austrian who pushed for the Carlsbad Decrees and was forced to resign in 1848.
question.clue: The Academic Legion forced this man's resignation during the Revolutions of 1848.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the Zionist Movement.
swap.text: This man declared that the Dreyfus Affair inspired him to establish the World Zionist Organization that encourages Jewish immigration to Palestine.
swap.clue: With Max Norday, this man established the Basel Program, through which the Russian faction shot down the Uganda Plan put forward by this man.

question.text: This nephew of Franz Josef became heir presumptive after the suicide of Crown Prince Rudolf and his own father's death. His assassination by Bosnian nationalist Gavrilo Princip set off the July Crisis.
question.clue: This Archduke of Austria, a nephew of Franz Joseph I.

swap.leadin: This empire was founded in the 1867 Ausgleich ("OWSS-glykh") and was dissolved in the Treaties of Saint Germain and Trianon ("TREE-uh-non").
swap.text: Name this empire that was first ruled by Franz Josef I.
swap.answerHtml: Austria-Hungary [or Austro-Hungarian Empire or Österreichisch-Ungarische Monarchie or Osztrák-Magyar Monarchia; prompt on dual monarchy; do not accept “Austria” or “Hungary” alone]
swap.clue: This empire formed after the Ausgleich, which made Franz Joseph I its first emperor.

question.text: This author of Der Judenstaat opposed the Uganda Project and established the First Zionist Congress.
question.clue: He could not overcome the opposition of the Russian faction of his confederates to the Uganda plan, nor could he talk the Ottoman Sultan into giving him what he wanted.

swap.leadin: After World War II, this event led to the formation of the "victim theory."
swap.text: Name this event translated as "connection" that Karl Schuschnigg failed to prevent. An original language term is required.
swap.clue: Kurt von Schuschnigg was replaced by Arthur Seyss-Inquart the day before this event, which gathered 99.7% approval in a plebiscite a month after it happened.

question.leadin: This ruler's foreign minister was Prince Felix of Schwarzenberg.
question.text: Name this ruler whose son Crown Prince Rudolf committed suicide in the Mayerling Incident. A member of the League of Three Emperors, this man named his nephew, the husband of Countess Sophie, as his heir.
question.answerHtml: Franz Joseph I of Austria [or Francis Joseph I]
question.clue: The Fundamental Articles of his minister of commerce and agriculture Albert Schaffle was denounced by German nationalists, and he appeared beside Alexander II in Berlin in 1873 in support of the Dreikaiserbund.

swap.leadin: Paul McCartney led a 30-superstar "Rockestra" during relief concerts for Cambodia at this politician's suggestion.
swap.text: Name this politician who was the target of an expose written by Alfred Worm for Profil magazine. This leader succeeded U Thant ("ooh tant") as United Nations Secretary General.
swap.clue: His service in the Kozara mountains involved a massacre of Yugoslavs, and he was also a senior lieutenant during the deportation of forty thousand Jews from Salonika.

question.leadin: In a 1783 declaration issued at Czernowitz, this Holy Roman Emperor abolished slavery in the Bukovina.
question.text: Name this emperor whose Patent of Toleration granted Christians religious freedom, which was extended to Jews in the Edict of Tolerance. This emperor's inebriated soldiers drank schnapps during a disaster at Karansebes ("KAW-rahn-seb-esh").
question.clue: His first wife Isabella of Parma died of smallpox long before that blunder in the Battle of Karansebes.

swap.leadin: A minister of this ruler freed peasants from their compulsory robota labor by breaking up church-owned estates in a process known as "Raabization."
swap.text: Name this ruler who also introduced one of the first compulsory public school systems. This ruler was officially designated as heir in an edict issued by Charles VI.
swap.answerHtml: Maria Theresa of Austria [or Maria Theresa Walburgia Amalia Christina]
swap.clue: Wenzel Kaunitz failed to persuade this monarch to not reclaim Silesia from Frederick II.

question.text: Germany's World War I version of an entrenching tool, called a Feldspaten, was similar to the MPL-50.Feldspatens were manufactured by this Austrian weapons manufacturer known for their easy-to-use handguns.

swap.leadin: This man founded the Fatherland's Front and promulgated the May Constitution.
swap.text: Identify this Austrian despot, who was assassinated in a Nazi plot and replaced with Kurt Schuschnigg.
swap.clue: This dictator absorbed the Heimwehr of Prince Starhemberg to establish the Fatherland Front, but was assassinated by Otto Planetta during the July Putsch.

question.text: The Interregnum was ended by the election of the first Habsburg emperor, a man of this name who destroyed many robber castles. The second emperor of this name patronized astronomers such as Kepler and Mannerist artists such as Arcimboldo.
question.clue: A ruler of this name greatly increased his territories after he defeated Ottokar II at the Battle of Marchfeld.

swap.leadin: Name these powerful women in 19th-century Europe.
swap.text: This wife of Emperor Franz Joseph of Austria-Hungary coerced her husband into the compromise that formed the Dual Monarchy. This Habsburg fashion icon was assassinated by the anarchist Luigi Lucheni in 1898.

question.text: The War of Austrian Succession was fought over the right of this monarch to ascend to the Austrian throne, which went against Salic Law and was supported by the Pragmatic Sanction of 1713.

swap.leadin: After this event, Count Eduard Taaffe claimed that a man died "due to a rupture of an aneurism of the heart."
swap.text: What event was a murder-suicide in which a man shot his lover, Mary Vetsera, and then killed himself while staying at a hunting lodge in the village that lends its name to this event?
swap.clue: Ida von Ferenczy was drafted to break the news of this event to Empress Elizabeth.
